title: Broadly prevent cardiac injury from cancer treatment without weakening cancer control

concept.text: The innovation would protect the heart across several major classes of cancer treatment while preserving those treatments’ ability to control cancer. Protection would need to prevent clinically important injury during treatment and delayed damage that emerges afterward. The goal extends beyond detecting early warning signs: patients would retain better cardiac health because injury was prevented.

Cancer treatments can damage the heart through different direct and indirect mechanisms, producing reversible or permanent injury. Broad protection therefore need not come from one drug or one molecular mechanism. As a proposed design, a coordinated set of complementary interventions could satisfy the concept if it reliably protected defined treatment and patient groups without shielding tumors, interfering with anticancer therapy, or introducing unacceptable harm.

significance.text: Effective protection across major cardiotoxic treatment classes would be a major enabling advance in cardio-oncology. Its direct benefit would be fewer treatment-related cardiac injuries and, if demonstrated clinically, fewer cases of heart failure and associated illness. The supplied review describes cardiac dysfunction as a complication that can affect quality of life, treatment efficacy and overall survival; it does not establish a numerical estimate of the benefit a future broad protective platform would deliver.

A plausible downstream consequence is that more patients could receive indicated cancer treatment with fewer cardiac interruptions or modifications. This is an inference from the documented relationship between cardiac management and treatment continuity, rather than a demonstrated result of broad prevention. Improved cancer survival, delivery of full-dose treatment in every patient, and reductions in overall mortality would each require separate evidence. Other treatment toxicities, cancer resistance and patient-specific constraints would remain relevant even if cardiac protection succeeded.

As an impact judgment, the transformative feature is the breadth and durability of protection combined with preserved cancer efficacy. Better surveillance, favorable biomarker changes, or an improvement confined to an already protected subgroup could be useful advances without fulfilling that larger capability. The supplied evidence does not establish a historical ranking for this innovation or support describing it as protection against every present and future cancer therapy.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is dependable prevention across heterogeneous treatment mechanisms and patient populations. Evidence that an intervention protects against one therapy cannot establish protection against other therapies with different injury pathways. Engineering a broad approach requires matching protective interventions to relevant mechanisms and treatment contexts while maintaining benefit across the populations in which they would be used.

A central biological and pharmacological barrier is protecting cardiac tissue without diminishing anticancer activity. This is a design requirement, not an assertion that all protective agents also protect tumors. The review discusses historical concerns about dexrazoxane interfering with chemotherapy and reports that more recent analyses have not substantiated those concerns in selected populations. That experience supports testing compatibility directly; it does not establish compatibility for every protective intervention, cancer or treatment regimen.

A further barrier is demonstrating durable clinical benefit rather than only favorable measurements. The review identifies heterogeneous studies, limited long-term evidence, and reliance on left ventricular ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain, which measure aspects of cardiac pumping and deformation. Improvements in these measures do not by themselves establish fewer heart-failure events, hospitalizations or deaths. Trials must also capture delayed injury and distinguish lasting protection from an early change that does not persist.

current_state.text: The supplied evidence centers on Michele Migliari and colleagues’ narrative review, “Current strategies for prevention of cancer therapy-related cardiotoxicity: pharmacological, non-pharmacological and emerging approaches,” published in Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine on 23 October 2025, DOI 10.3389/fcvm.2025.1668308. Its non-systematic literature search covered PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science through June 2025. It documents selected protective approaches and evidence gaps rather than a comprehensive assessment of every intervention.

Protection is already supported in selected settings, particularly dexrazoxane during anthracycline treatment. The review reports robust protection in anthracycline-treated patients, discusses randomized evidence in selected populations, and describes dexrazoxane as the only FDA-approved agent in its cardioprotection discussion. These are findings reported by the 2025 review; they should not be extended to all cancer treatments or treated as a separately verified account of regulatory status in November 2026. Evidence for several other approaches is less conclusive.

The review’s evidence base is heterogeneous and often uses surrogate cardiac endpoints. Selected-setting efficacy therefore does not establish broad protection, durable prevention of clinical heart failure, or preserved cancer efficacy in every population. The review does not demonstrate a universal protective platform, but that limitation is not proof that no broader approach exists elsewhere in the literature.

According to the supplied validated review and source index, the article’s identity was verified and its complete text and references were retained without reported truncation or extraction problems. The underlying trials were not separately supplied or inspected in that review. The supplied freshness record is empty, so this material cannot establish the complete state of the field on 1 November 2026 or determine whether evidence published after the June 2025 search changed the assessment.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: randomized studies across several prespecified major cardiotoxic treatment classes and cancer populations should show clinically meaningful reductions in cardiac injury and heart failure. Studies should define the outcomes and minimum worthwhile effects in advance, with clinical events carrying more weight than isolated biomarker or imaging changes. The review’s call for larger international randomized trials and longer follow-up motivates this proposal, but these completion criteria are not an established consensus standard.
completion_criteria.label: Randomized trials demonstrate clinically meaningful cardiac protection across treatment classes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed cancer-control requirement: trials should assess relevant oncologic outcomes and exclude a prespecified clinically unacceptable loss of efficacy. Simply finding no statistically significant difference in cancer outcomes would be insufficient if the study could not rule out a consequential loss. The acceptable margin, endpoints and observation period would need justification for each cancer and treatment setting; none is established by the supplied record.
completion_criteria.label: Trials exclude prespecified clinically unacceptable losses of cancer-control efficacy

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and reproducibility requirement: follow-up should be long enough to evaluate delayed cardiac injury, persistence of benefit and adverse effects. Findings should be reproduced across independent studies or adequately diverse multicenter settings, with explicit reporting of treatment regimens, patient characteristics and limits of applicability. The evidence should make clear which groups benefit, where protection remains uncertain, and whether practical delivery requirements restrict use.
completion_criteria.label: Durable cardiac protection reproduces with explicit reporting of applicability limits

completion_criteria.text: Proposed scope boundary: success could be achieved by multiple complementary interventions rather than one universal agent. Demonstration across a defined set of major therapies would establish breadth within that tested scope, not literal universality. Specific populations, effect thresholds, follow-up durations and cancer-control margins remain to be defined; no finite trial program can guarantee protection against every present and future therapy.
completion_criteria.label: Protection spans defined major therapies with explicitly bounded scope

related_concepts.text: Roster comparison: CAR-01, regenerating a severely damaged adult human heart, addresses repair after injury; CAR-13 addresses prevention of treatment-related injury. CAR-03, a durable and broadly affordable total artificial heart; CAR-04, a dependable supply of transplantable animal hearts; and CAR-07, a transplantable engineered living human heart, offer distinct replacement routes for severe cardiac failure. Effective prevention could reduce some demand for repair or replacement without supplying those capabilities.

Roster comparison: CAR-05 seeks direct, durable correction of inherited heart disease in the beating heart. Its disease origins and correction objective differ from preventing injury caused by cancer treatment. CAR-08 seeks durable reversal of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction; preventing treatment-related cardiac dysfunction does not establish reversal of that syndrome across its major subtypes.

Roster comparison: CAR-06 concerns predicting and preventing most preventable sudden cardiac deaths, while CAR-09 seeks a durable, non-ablative cure for atrial fibrillation. These concepts overlap with CAR-13 where treatment-related cardiac injury contributes to rhythm problems or sudden-death risk. Reduced cardiac injury alone would not demonstrate either broad sudden-death prevention or a durable atrial-fibrillation cure.

Roster comparison: CAR-02 addresses reversal of advanced atherosclerosis throughout the arterial tree, and CAR-12 addresses detection of actionable coronary plaque risk before a first clinical event. CAR-10 concerns reversing established calcific aortic stenosis without valve replacement, and CAR-11 concerns reversal of pulmonary arterial hypertension and its cardiovascular consequences. These remain distinct vascular, valvular and pulmonary vascular capabilities. A protective cancer-treatment strategy would need its own evidence rather than inheriting efficacy from advances in any of them.

change_log.reason: The transformative capability does not require one universal drug or mechanism, and heterogeneous injury mechanisms favor an adaptable scope.

change_log.change: Expanded the explanation of early and delayed injury, anticancer compatibility, and the distinction between prevention and surveillance.
change_log.reason: These scientific distinctions explain what the innovation must accomplish beyond detecting or managing toxicity.

change_log.change: Anchored current-state claims to the October 2025 narrative review and its June 2025 search boundary.
change_log.reason: Publication date, search coverage and full-text availability do not establish freshness through November 2026.

change_log.change: Retained selected-setting dexrazoxane evidence while qualifying its scope and attributing the regulatory statement to the review.
change_log.reason: Evidence in anthracycline-treated populations does not establish universal protection or independently verify later regulatory status.

change_log.change: Distinguished surrogate cardiac measurements from clinical outcomes and direct benefits from conditional downstream effects.
change_log.reason: Imaging improvements do not alone establish fewer clinical events, and broad cardioprotection does not automatically establish improved cancer survival or full-dose treatment for every patient.

change_log.change: Operationalized the proposed completion criteria with prespecified effects, cancer-control margins, delayed follow-up and reproducibility.
change_log.reason: Vague requirements for substantial benefit, long-term safety and no meaningful loss of efficacy need explicit definitions; failure to detect a cancer-outcome difference is insufficient to establish preserved efficacy.

change_log.change: Added explicit distinctions from the other supplied roster entries and preserved evidence-access boundaries.
change_log.reason: Related clinical objectives do not merge prevention with repair, replacement or disease reversal, and review-level evidence should not be presented as independently inspected trial evidence.

unresolved_issues: The supplied material does not establish whether evidence published after June 2025 changed the field’s state by 1 November 2026.
The treatment classes, cancer populations, minimum worthwhile cardiac effects, cancer-control margins and follow-up durations needed for a convincing broad demonstration remain undefined.
Underlying trials were not separately supplied or inspected in the validated review, limiting independent assessment of their methods, effect sizes, safety and generalizability.
The supplied evidence does not identify a demonstrated intervention or combination that fulfills the proposed breadth, durability and preserved-cancer-control requirements.
The magnitude of population benefit, effects on cancer-treatment continuity, and any improvement in cancer survival or overall mortality remain unestablished.

brief.title: Heart protection during and after cancer treatment
possible: People receiving cancer treatment could keep their hearts healthier during treatment and long afterward, while their treatment remains effective against cancer. Protection would cover several major kinds of cancer treatment.
why: Preventing heart injury would spare patients illness and protect their quality of life. It could also mean fewer interruptions or changes to cancer treatment because of heart problems.

sources.showed: Their review found strong support for dexrazoxane, a protective drug used with anthracyclines, a family of chemotherapy drugs. Several other approaches improved heart measurements without proving fewer serious heart problems.
sources.quote: Exercise and nutrition provide functional and quality of life benefits, while several novel strategies remain exploratory.
sources.cited_for: Heart protection already works in selected treatment settings.
sources.not_established: The review does not establish lasting prevention of heart failure across major cancer treatments with cancer control preserved.

sources.showed: Lisinopril and carvedilol reduced declines in heart pumping in women given anthracyclines plus trastuzumab, a breast cancer drug. Across the full trial, heart injury rates were similar, but the drugs reduced treatment interruptions.
sources.quote: Being on an active drug resulted in fewer interruptions in trastuzumab in the whole study population and in the anthracycline cohort.
sources.cited_for: Protective drugs can preserve heart pumping and reduce treatment interruptions in a defined breast cancer group.
sources.not_established: The trial does not establish broad protection, lasting prevention of heart failure, or preserved cancer control.

sources.showed: A small breast cancer trial found that shaped radiation beams with breath holding reduced heart exposure and better preserved heart pumping. Lung blood flow, or perfusion, and lung function did not differ.
sources.quote: No differences were found for lung perfusion or function.
sources.cited_for: Changing radiation delivery can reduce heart exposure and improve a measure of heart pumping.
sources.not_established: The main measure of heart blood flow showed no benefit, and the trial did not establish fewer later cases of heart failure.

shown: Protection works in selected settings. Migliari and colleagues’ review found strong support for dexrazoxane during anthracycline chemotherapy. Guglin and colleagues found that protective drugs helped preserve heart pumping in a defined breast cancer group.

Jagsi and colleagues’ small radiation trial also found better preservation of heart pumping. These results support pieces of the goal, but lasting protection across major cancer treatments with cancer control preserved remains unproven.
missing: Reliable protection across cancer treatments that damage the heart in different ways and across the patient groups who receive them.
Trials that rule out a meaningful loss of cancer control when heart protection is added.
Lasting reductions in heart injury and heart failure, including damage that appears after cancer treatment ends.

milestones.label: Trials find fewer heart injuries across treatment classes
milestones.explanation: Trials that randomly assign treatments would have to show worthwhile reductions in heart injury and heart failure across major treatment classes. This would establish benefits beyond better scans or blood tests.

milestones.label: Trials rule out unacceptable losses of cancer control
milestones.explanation: Trials would have to rule out a loss of cancer control beyond a limit justified in advance for each setting. This would establish that heart protection preserves the cancer treatment’s benefit.

milestones.label: Lasting protection repeats, with clear limits on who benefits
milestones.explanation: Independent studies or diverse hospitals would have to reproduce lasting protection, track delayed injury and harms, and identify who benefits. This would establish durability and where protection applies.

milestones.label: Protection covers a defined range of major therapies
milestones.explanation: An approach, potentially combining complementary interventions, would have to protect across a defined set of major therapies. This would establish breadth within a clear tested scope.

uncertain: Which treatment classes and patient groups would be enough to establish broad protection remains undefined.
The minimum worthwhile heart benefit, acceptable cancer-control loss and necessary follow-up remain to be agreed.
Whether broad heart protection would improve cancer survival or overall survival remains unknown.

page.title: Primary prevention of cancer therapy-related cardiotoxicity
page.definition: Primary prevention starts before treatment-related heart injury develops. The goal is fewer cases of clinical heart disease during and after anthracycline chemotherapy, HER2-targeted therapy and radiotherapy to the chest, while preserving cancer control. Dexrazoxane already reduces heart failure in some patients receiving anthracyclines. HER2 is human epidermal growth factor receptor 2, the target of drugs such as trastuzumab.

goal.need: After breast radiotherapy, the rate of major coronary events rose 7.4% per gray of mean heart dose, with excess risk extending into the third decade. Heart protection can also help patients stay on treatment. In a trastuzumab trial, 16.3% had a treatment interruption on preventive heart medicines versus 26.3% on placebo. A smaller decline in the heart’s pumping function alone does not establish that fewer patients develop heart failure. Simply limiting chemotherapy or reducing radiation to lymph nodes can compromise cancer treatment.

figures.caption: Breast-radiotherapy case–control study published on 14 March 2013.
rows: Coronary-event rate increase per 1 Gy mean heart dose
figures.note: Major coronary events comprised myocardial infarction, coronary revascularization or death from ischemic heart disease. The estimate is a relative rate increase.

completion.title: Clinical cardiac injury falls across the listed therapies without unacceptable loss of cancer control.
completion.criterion: For each listed treatment class, randomized evidence meets prespecified superiority criteria for clinically manifest cardiac injury and prespecified noninferiority criteria for cancer control during treatment and subsequent follow-up. Noninferiority excludes the protocol's unacceptable loss of cancer efficacy. Published regimen-specific protocols set the endpoints, margins and observation periods; distinct protective interventions may serve different classes. The evidence includes delayed cardiac outcomes rather than imaging changes alone. No common numerical margin or follow-up duration is assigned across classes.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; synthesis of NIH goals and regimen-specific trial tests, without an external cross-class completion standard.
completion.basis: NIH names the joint cardiac and cancer goal. Individual protocols define their own tests. In breast radiotherapy, RadComp compares 10-year major cardiovascular events and separately tests whether the excess in five-year local-regional recurrence with protons stays within 3.8 percentage points. In lymphoma, ANTICIPATE pairs a 12-month cardiac imaging endpoint with a 10-percentage-point margin for complete metabolic remission. The requirement for clinical cardiac benefit and preserved cancer control in every listed class is an Atlas criterion.

milestones.title: A cardioprotective intervention reproduces its preclinical benefit in human tissue or human-derived cells.
milestones.criterion: Validate the intervention’s protective effect in human tissue or human-derived cells relevant to the cardiac injury caused by the specified cancer treatment. NCI recommends human-model validation and gives no minimum effect size.
milestones.set_by: National Cancer Institute, funding announcement PAR-25-145, Specific Areas of Research Interest; a recommendation for human-model validation, not a numerical efficacy cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: validate their findings in human tissue or human-derived cells with direct applicability to human conditions.

milestones.title: A cardioprotective drug reaches a human dose suitable for phase 2 testing.
milestones.criterion: Identify a dose for further clinical testing and establish that phase 1 exposure does not reveal toxicity that precludes phase 2. Acceptability is assessed for the drug and schedule under study.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, The FDA's Drug Review Process; this drug-development stage applies directly to pharmacological interventions.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 2 studies begin if Phase 1 studies don't reveal unacceptable toxicity.

milestones.title: A protective intervention reduces its prespecified cardiac endpoint in a randomized trial.
milestones.criterion: Meet the randomized trial’s prespecified superiority test on its primary cardiac endpoint. In NCT01009918, compare each preventive drug with placebo on the proportion with cardiotoxicity by the end of trastuzumab treatment or week 52, at one-sided α = 0.025. An event is an absolute fall from baseline in left ventricular ejection fraction of ≥10 percentage points, or ≥5 points if the follow-up value is <50%. Other regimens use their own prespecified endpoints and significance levels.
milestones.set_by: NCT01009918 investigators, SCUSF 0806 protocol version 6.0 and published primary analysis, for trastuzumab-treated breast cancer
milestones.threshold_quote: an absolute decrease ≥ 10% in LVEF at study follow-up OR an absolute decrease ≥ 5% in LVEF if it is < 50%

milestones.title: An intervention meets both cardiac superiority and cancer-control noninferiority tests.
milestones.criterion: Meet both prespecified tests. In ANTICIPATE’s published lymphoma design, dexrazoxane must reduce the incidence of a fall of ≥10 percentage points in left ventricular ejection fraction to <50% within 12 months of randomization, at one-sided α = 0.025. Analyze as randomized, excluding patients switched to DA-EPOCH-R chemotherapy. In the as-treated population, complete metabolic remission on PET-CT 6–8 weeks after the last R-CHOP cycle must meet a 10-percentage-point noninferiority margin at one-sided α = 0.05.
milestones.set_by: HOVON 170 DLBCL-ANTICIPATE consortium, published phase III design; the numerical criteria apply to anthracycline-treated lymphoma, with separate protocols required for other cases.
milestones.threshold_quote: superiority of addition of dexrazoxane on the primary endpoint and non-inferiority on the co-primary endpoint are both demonstrated.

milestones.title: A protective intervention reduces clinical cardiac events over its protocol-defined long-term follow-up.
milestones.criterion: Show superiority on the randomized trial’s prespecified delayed clinical cardiac endpoint. In DBCG PROTON, compare proton with photon breast radiotherapy on time to the first ischemic or valvular heart disease event, using a log-rank test at α = 0.05. Report cumulative incidence at 10 years after trial entry. Recurrence and survival are secondary endpoints.
milestones.set_by: Danish Breast Cancer Group, DBCG PROTON protocol version 1.3, 4 January 2024, for adjuvant breast radiotherapy
milestones.threshold_quote: ischaemic heart disease and valvular disease at 10 years

milestones.title: A postmastectomy proton plan limits mean heart dose to 1.5% of prescription while covering the target.
milestones.criterion: For postmastectomy proton treatment of the chest wall and regional nodes under MC1631, mean heart dose must be ≤1.5% of the prescribed dose. At least 95% of the clinical target volume must receive ≥95% of the prescribed dose, and the dose to the hottest 0.01 cm³ of that volume must be ≤110%. Evaluate target coverage with setup shifts of ±5 mm and proton range uncertainty of ±3%.
milestones.set_by: Mayo Clinic MC1631 investigators, postmastectomy proton radiotherapy protocol NCT02783690

not_found: No external cross-class completion standard specifying treatment coverage, cardiac benefit, cancer-control margin and follow-up was found.
No result jointly establishing clinical cardiac benefit and cancer-control noninferiority across all three listed classes was found.
No published joint primary result for ANTICIPATE or 10-year primary cardiac result for DBCG PROTON or RadComp was found.

results.finding: Lisinopril and carvedilol were tested at 10 mg daily in 468 women receiving trastuzumab.
results.detail: The randomized trial used both doses through trastuzumab treatment. Potentially related side effects were more prevalent with lisinopril; the reported experience supports tolerability at the tested doses.
results.quote: Low doses for both lisinopril and carvedilol (10 mg daily for both) were chosen for this normotensive patient population.

results.finding: In 468 randomized women, carvedilol did not significantly reduce cardiotoxicity overall versus placebo; adjusted one-tailed p=0.163.
results.detail: The overall prespecified primary comparison was negative. Cardiotoxicity-free survival favored both drugs in the anthracycline-exposed subgroup, but subgroup effects were a secondary analysis.
results.quote: Using the logistic regression model to adjust for anthracycline strata and baseline LVEF, the one-tailed p-values were 0.163 and 0.187 for the comparisons of carvedilol and lisinopril to placebo, respectively.

results.finding: Among 468 women receiving trastuzumab, carvedilol versus placebo yielded an adjusted one-sided p=0.163 for the primary cardiotoxicity endpoint.
results.detail: All participants received trastuzumab. Anthracycline exposure defined a stratum for the trastuzumab cardiotoxicity analysis.
results.quote: Using the logistic regression model to adjust for anthracycline strata and baseline LVEF, the one-tailed p-values were 0.163 and 0.187 for the comparisons of carvedilol and lisinopril to placebo, respectively.

results.finding: Among 54 analyzed breast radiotherapy patients, IMRT with breath hold did not improve primary cardiac perfusion at the stricter threshold (p=0.70).
results.quote: SPECT revealed no differences in perfusion defects in the left anterior descending coronary artery territory, the study’s primary endpoint, but did reveal statistically significant differences (p=0.02) in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), a secondary endpoint.

results.finding: In a 54-patient breast radiotherapy comparison, the IMRT arm’s mean whole-heart dose was 2.35 Gy.
In human stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (n = 8), 1 μM indisulam gave the greatest rescue of viability after doxorubicin exposure.
results.detail: The text reports the best-performing concentration. The size of the viability improvement is presented in Figure 3K.
results.quote: We then conducted doseresponse experiments and determined that 1 μM of indisulam exerted the highest rescue effect on DIC

results.finding: AICAR attenuated trastuzumab-induced loss of contractility in human cardiomyocytes from 3 donors during 7 days of co-treatment.
results.detail: The AICAR contraction-velocity assay used 50 and 100 μM. Rapamycin failed to rescue contraction velocity in the separate patient-derived assay.
results.quote: Indeed, we observed that the AMPK activator, AICAR, attenuated mitochondrial dysfunction and contractile dysfunction induced by trastuzumab in iPSC-CMs, suggesting that alterations in energy metabolism may play a key role in trastuzumab-induced cardiac dysfunction.

results.finding: Pravastatin and atorvastatin preserved nitric oxide production in human coronary artery endothelial cells exposed to 4 Gy across four independent experiments.
results.detail: Cells received either statin 18 hours before irradiation. Pravastatin also protected mitochondrial endpoints that remained impaired with atorvastatin.
results.quote: NO production by HCAECs after irradiation was significantly reduced at both time points, and this effect was abolished by pretreatment with statins

results.finding: Among 69 evaluable patients receiving postoperative proton breast or chest-wall and nodal radiotherapy, the median mean heart dose was 0.50 Gy (RBE).
results.detail: The study used a planning constraint of mean heart dose <1.5 Gy (RBE). The reported heart-dose median pools patients treated after mastectomy and patients with intact breasts.
results.quote: With regard to normal structures, the mean heart dose was a median of 0.50 Gy (RBE), and the mean LAD dose was a median of 1.16 Gy (RBE).

results.finding: Among 164 women receiving anthracyclines, dexrazoxane reduced cardiac events versus control (P < 0.001).
results.detail: The abstract reports both cardiac events and congestive heart failure and leaves their endpoint hierarchy unspecified.
results.quote: Compared with those receiving anthracycline alone, patients treated with dexrazoxane experienced significantly fewer cardiac events (39% versus 13%, P < 0.001) and a lower and less severe incidence of congestive heart failure (11% versus 1%, P < 0.05).

results.finding: In 164 women receiving anthracyclines, dexrazoxane reduced cardiac events (P < 0.001), with tumor response reported as unaffected.
results.detail: The abstract gives no tumor response rates or confidence interval for the between-group difference.
results.quote: Compared with those receiving anthracycline alone, patients treated with dexrazoxane experienced significantly fewer cardiac events (39% versus 13%, P < 0.001) and a lower and less severe incidence of congestive heart failure (11% versus 1%, P < 0.05). Tumor response rate was unaffected by dexrazoxane therapy.

results.finding: In PERSEPHONE, shorter trastuzumab reduced 12-month clinical cardiac dysfunction among 3962 assessed patients (p=0·00014).
results.detail: Clinical cardiac dysfunction included symptoms of cardiac disease, signs of congestive heart failure, or use of new cardiac medication.
results.quote: Clinical cardiac dysfunction was reported more commonly in the 12-month group (224 [11%] of 1968 patients) than in the 6-month group (155 [8%] of 1994 patients; p=0·00014;

results.finding: Among 4088 PERSEPHONE patients, shorter trastuzumab met the 4-year disease-free survival noninferiority test (p=0·011).
results.detail: The trial compared trastuzumab durations in early breast cancer. ANTICIPATE’s lymphoma-specific LVEF and PET-CT criteria apply to its dexrazoxane comparison.
results.quote: The HR for relapse or death with 6 months compared with 12 months trastuzumab was 1·07 (90% CI 0·93–1·24, non-inferiority p=0·011); this outcome met the prespecified definition of non-inferiority.

results.finding: A 25-patient doxorubicin study identified dexrazoxane 600 mg/m2 as the dose for further testing.
results.detail: Tolerability at the recommended dose was observed in three patients with better performance status and at most one prior chemotherapy regimen. Four of six previously treated patients had dose-limiting neutropenia at the same dose.
results.quote: We recommend that an ADR-529 dose of 600 mg/m2 be given with single-agent doxorubicin at a dose of 60 mg/m2 in future studies.

results.finding: In SAFE (n = 262), ramipril and bisoprolol each reduced the primary cardiac endpoint after anthracycline chemotherapy (both P < 0.001).
results.quote:
Subclinical cardiac damage occurred in 11.4% of patients receiving ramipril versus 39.3% without
ramipril (P < 0.001), and in 9.6% of patients receiving bisoprolol versus 43.5% without bisoprolol (P < 0.001).

results.finding: In 509 women with metastatic breast cancer, the cardiotoxicity hazard was higher with conventional than with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (HR 3.16).
results.detail: Cardiac events were based on LVEF reductions in relation to cumulative anthracycline dose. The abstract describes progression-free survival as comparable and gives no noninferiority margin.
results.quote: Overall risk of cardiotoxicity was significantly higher with doxorubicin than PLD (HR = 3.16; 95%CI 1.58-6.31; P <0.001).

results.finding: Among 164 children receiving doxorubicin, fewer serious cardiovascular events occurred with dexrazoxane (p=0.02).
results.detail: The composite included ischemic heart disease, cardiomyopathy, and stroke. Valve disease was analyzed separately. Median observation in the linked records was 676 days with dexrazoxane and 660 days without it.
results.quote: However, collectively, hard cardiovascular endpoints (cardiomyopathy, ischemic heart disease, stroke) occurred less commonly among randomized DRZ-assigned patients versus patients without DRZ (5.6% versus 17.6%; p=0.02).

results.finding: MC1631 postmastectomy proton radiotherapy (82 patients) achieved a median mean heart dose of 0.49 Gy.
results.detail: The arm medians establish heart sparing at the group level. The reported internal mammary node dose covers only part of the clinical target volume.
results.quote: The median mean heart dose for all 82 patients was 0.49 Gy.

definition = "Primary prevention starts before treatment-related heart injury develops. The goal is fewer cases of clinical heart disease during and after anthracycline chemotherapy, HER2-targeted therapy and radiotherapy to the chest, while preserving cancer control. Dexrazoxane already reduces heart failure in some patients receiving anthracyclines. HER2 is human epidermal growth factor receptor 2, the target of drugs such as trastuzumab.". Reason: A clinical example distinguishes protection already demonstrated for one anthracycline regimen from the goal across all three treatment classes.

goal.need = "After breast radiotherapy, the rate of major coronary events rose 7.4% per gray of mean heart dose, with excess risk extending into the third decade. Heart protection can also help patients stay on treatment. In a trastuzumab trial, 16.3% had a treatment interruption on preventive heart medicines versus 26.3% on placebo. A smaller decline in the heart\u2019s pumping function alone does not establish that fewer patients develop heart failure. Simply limiting chemotherapy or reducing radiation to lymph nodes can compromise cancer treatment.". Reason: The current rationale reports an imaging endpoint but omits the size of the late coronary risk, the effect on treatment interruptions and the cost of reducing cancer treatment exposure.

add statement by International Guideline Harmonization Group for Late Effects of Childhood Cancer, 2022: "Administration of dexrazoxane is reasonable in children". Reason: The pediatric guideline identifies a patient group for whom a professional body has endorsed primary cardioprotection and specifies the limit of that recommendation.

edit completion: basis = "NIH names the joint cardiac and cancer goal. Individual protocols define their own tests. In breast radiotherapy, RadComp compares 10-year major cardiovascular events and separately tests whether the excess in five-year local-regional recurrence with protons stays within 3.8 percentage points. In lymphoma, ANTICIPATE pairs a 12-month cardiac imaging endpoint with a 10-percentage-point margin for complete metabolic remission. The requirement for clinical cardiac benefit and preserved cancer control in every listed class is an Atlas criterion."; refs = [4, 7, 21, 23]. Reason: RadComp supplies a direct protocol precedent for testing delayed clinical cardiac events and cancer-control noninferiority in the same treatment class.

edit m1: criterion = "Validate the intervention\u2019s protective effect in human tissue or human-derived cells relevant to the cardiac injury caused by the specified cancer treatment. NCI recommends human-model validation and gives no minimum effect size."; threshold_quote = "validate their findings in human tissue or human-derived cells with direct applicability to human conditions."; threshold_ref = 5; refs = [5, 9, 15]. Reason: The laboratory criterion currently includes an individual experiment’s doses, replicate count and results, none of which NCI sets as a threshold.

edit m2: title = "A cardioprotective drug reaches a human dose suitable for phase 2 testing."; criterion = "Identify a dose for further clinical testing and establish that phase 1 exposure does not reveal toxicity that precludes phase 2. Acceptability is assessed for the drug and schedule under study."; threshold_quote = "Phase 2 studies begin if Phase 1 studies don't reveal unacceptable toxicity."; threshold_ref = 10; refs = [10, 11]. Reason: The FDA transition applies to drugs, and the dose and adherence observed in a carvedilol trial are results rather than phase 1 requirements.

add milestone after m2: "A postmastectomy proton plan limits mean heart dose to 1.5% of prescription while covering the target.". Reason: Radiotherapy has a measurable planning stage in which the heart-dose limit and the dose required at the cancer target must both be met.

edit m3: criterion = "Meet the randomized trial\u2019s prespecified superiority test on its primary cardiac endpoint. In NCT01009918, compare each preventive drug with placebo on the proportion with cardiotoxicity by the end of trastuzumab treatment or week 52, at one-sided \u03b1 = 0.025. An event is an absolute fall from baseline in left ventricular ejection fraction of \u226510 percentage points, or \u22655 points if the follow-up value is <50%. Other regimens use their own prespecified endpoints and significance levels."; set_by = "NCT01009918 investigators, SCUSF 0806 protocol version 6.0 and published primary analysis, for trastuzumab-treated breast cancer"; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "an absolute decrease \u2265 10% in LVEF at study follow-up OR an absolute decrease \u2265 5% in LVEF if it is < 50%"; threshold_ref = 25; refs = [25, 2, 12, 18]. Reason: The registered trastuzumab protocol counts falls of exactly 10 or 5 percentage points, which the current strict inequalities exclude.

edit m4: criterion = "Meet both prespecified tests. In ANTICIPATE\u2019s published lymphoma design, dexrazoxane must reduce the incidence of a fall of \u226510 percentage points in left ventricular ejection fraction to <50% within 12 months of randomization, at one-sided \u03b1 = 0.025. Analyze as randomized, excluding patients switched to DA-EPOCH-R chemotherapy. In the as-treated population, complete metabolic remission on PET-CT 6\u20138 weeks after the last R-CHOP cycle must meet a 10-percentage-point noninferiority margin at one-sided \u03b1 = 0.05."; threshold_quote = "superiority of addition of dexrazoxane on the primary endpoint and non-inferiority on the co-primary endpoint are both demonstrated."; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7, 14]. Reason: The criterion mixes trial status with the two efficacy tests and omits the populations in which the protocol evaluates them.

edit m5: criterion = "Show superiority on the randomized trial\u2019s prespecified delayed clinical cardiac endpoint. In DBCG PROTON, compare proton with photon breast radiotherapy on time to the first ischemic or valvular heart disease event, using a log-rank test at \u03b1 = 0.05. Report cumulative incidence at 10 years after trial entry. Recurrence and survival are secondary endpoints."; set_by = "Danish Breast Cancer Group, DBCG PROTON protocol version 1.3, 4 January 2024, for adjuvant breast radiotherapy"; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "ischaemic heart disease and valvular disease at 10 years"; threshold_ref = 21; refs = [21]. Reason: DBCG PROTON version 1.3 specifies the cardiac comparison and its analysis directly, so the criterion can use the amendment and omit the result-search history.

structure = parallel. Reason: A radiation plan can meet heart-dose limits independently of drug dose-finding, and a single randomized trial can assess delayed cardiac events and cancer control together.
